# IEA "Energy and AI" (2025) — Energy supply for AI

## Key figures
- Global electricity generation to supply data centres grows from 460 TWh in 2024 to over 1,000 TWh in 2030 and 1,300 TWh in 2035 (Base Case).
- 2024 fuel mix of electricity physically consumed by data centres: coal ~30% (largest source; highest contribution in China), renewables ~27%, natural gas 26%, nuclear 15%.
- Renewables are the fastest-growing source: generation grows at 22% annually 2024–2030, meeting nearly 50% of growth in data centre electricity demand.
- Natural gas + coal together meet over 40% of additional electricity demand from data centres until 2030.
- After 2030 SMRs enter the mix; hyperscalers are key corporate backers. By 2035 the rise in renewables and nuclear leads to an absolute decline in coal-fired generation for data centre operations.
- CO2 emissions from data centre electricity peak at ~320 Mt CO2 by 2030, then shallow decline to ~300 Mt CO2 by 2035. Data centres rise from ~1% of global electricity generation today to 3% in 2030; less than 1% of total global CO2 emissions.
- United States: natural gas is the biggest source (>40% share), renewables 24% (mostly solar PV and wind), nuclear ~20%, coal ~15%. Natural gas adds over 130 TWh of annual generation until 2030; renewables add 110 TWh 2024–2030. Tech companies have plans to finance more than 20 GW of SMRs. By 2035 low-emissions sources account for over half of the US data centre electricity supply mix.
- China: coal dominates with a near 70% share (data centres mostly in the east), renewables nearly 20%, nuclear close to 10%, gas the remainder. 2024–2030: coal adds nearly 90 TWh/year; renewables add nearly 90 TWh. After 2030 SMRs significantly boost the nuclear share; by 2035 renewables + nuclear make up nearly 60% of China's data centre electricity supply, pushing coal into decline.
- Europe: renewables + nuclear combined share rising to 85% by 2030. Japan + Korea ~5% of global data centre demand; renewables + nuclear ~60% in 2030 (up from 35% today).
- Sensitivity cases: High Efficiency ~1,100 TWh by 2035 (>15% lower); Headwinds 790 TWh (>40% lower); Lift-Off nearly 2,000 TWh by 2035 (45% higher). In Lift-Off, 2024–2030 nearly 50% of additional electricity comes from fossil fuels; gas grows ~1.5x faster, coal 2x faster (China most of the coal increase). Fossil fuels ~40% of total data centre electricity in 2035 across all cases.
- In the Lift-Off Case, CO2 emissions keep rising into the early 2030s, peaking at nearly 1.5x the Base Case maximum.
